To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the learned representations are invariant to inter-instance variations (different instances but same class) and intra-instance variations (different viewpoints of the object); 2) the learned representations generalize better to other tasks (object detection, segmentation, etc.); 3) the learned representations can be transferred to other tasks (surface normal estimation).

(i) we can obtain a large dataset with millions of objects and hundreds of thousands of categories from videos, (ii) we can learn representations that are invariant to both instance and viewpoint variations, and (iii) these representations can be used in a wide variety of recognition tasks, including object detection, surface normal estimation, and semantic segmentation.

(i) we can learn visual representations with a single network that is invariant to both inter-instance and intra-instance variations, (ii) we can achieve state-of-the-art performance on object detection and surface normal estimation with only self-supervised training, and (iii) the learned representations are useful in a wide range of vision tasks
